results.label: prop:buneman
results.name: Buneman's theorem
results.tested: a set of non-trivial splits is a stemma's split set iff pairwise compatible, the tree unique up to isomorphism

checks.instances: 300 random stemmata ($4\le n\le10$, 188 non-binary) and 300 random compatible sets
checks.result: split sets pairwise compatible; split set $\to$ tree $\to$ split set exact, internal degrees $\ge3$, rebuilt tree isomorphic to the original as a leaf-labelled tree, in all

results.label: lem:facts
results.name: Two counting facts
results.tested: size $n-3$ and maximality of binary split sets; at most $n-3$ splits in any compatible set

checks.instances: 400 random binary trees, $4\le n\le9$, all splits scanned per tree; sampled compatible sets
checks.result: size $n-3$, maximality and the bound $n-3$ hold in all

results.label: lem:exclusive
results.name: Exclusivity
results.tested: splits (and clusters) proposed by one unit are pairwise compatible

checks.instances: 400 random collations, $4\le n\le9$, multistate units with random illegibility (6{,}141 units)
checks.result: all 3{,}791 same-unit split pairs compatible and all 1{,}716 cluster pairs laminar; 10{,}433 conflicting pairs across units (control)

results.label: thm:universal
results.name: Universality
results.tested: the construction realises a given graph as the conflict graph of distinct non-trivial splits

checks.instances: 300 random graphs, $2\le|V|\le8$
checks.result: all realised ($4|E|+2|V|+2$ witnesses, distinct non-trivial splits, conflict graph equal to $H$)

results.label: cor:nphard
results.name: NP-hardness
results.tested: the construction preserves vertex weights and MWIS values, so it is a reduction

checks.instances: 250 random graphs, $2\le|V|\le10$, integer weights $1$--$20$
checks.result: MWIS of $H$ (brute force) equals the maximum-weight compatible set of the constructed splits, same value and same optimal sets, in all; $4|E|+2|V|+2$ witnesses

results.label: prop:triple
results.name: Pairs exact, triples not
results.tested: overlap-compatible pairs are completable; triples need not be

checks.instances: every partial split on $n=4,5,6$ witnesses (domains of size $4$ to $n$)
checks.result: all overlap-compatible pairs completable; 0 obstructing triples on $4$ witnesses, 200 on $5$; the triple $p,q,r$ pairwise compatible and not completable

checks.instances: proper partial splits on five witnesses, all triples
checks.result: 140 obstructing triples of quartets (expected $140$)

results.label: thm:cutting
results.name: Cutting planes
results.tested: the lazy-cut loop returns a maximum jointly completable family

checks.instances: 60 random weighted families of partial splits, $n=5,6$
checks.result: cut loop reaches the brute-force optimum in all (40 cuts in total)

results.label: lem:hall
results.name: Displacement matching
results.tested: for compatible $S\neq\T$: $A\neq\emptyset$, $|B|\le|A|$ and a matching of $B$ into $A$ by conflicts

checks.instances: 3{,}815 sampled pairs $(T,S)$, $4\le n\le9$
checks.result: $A\neq\emptyset$, $|B|\le|A|$ and the matching exist in all

results.label: thm:local
results.name: Local separation
results.tested: under the local hypothesis the true set is the unique maximum-weight compatible set

checks.instances: 80 random binary trees, $n=5..7$, weights meeting the local hypothesis; all compatible sets enumerated
checks.result: the true set is the unique optimum in all

results.label: thm:global
results.name: Global separation
results.tested: under the global hypothesis the true set is the unique maximum-weight compatible set

checks.instances: 80 random binary trees, $n=5..7$, weights meeting the global hypothesis; all compatible sets enumerated
checks.result: the true set is the unique optimum in all

results.label: prop:threshold
results.name: Non-binary threshold
results.tested: with false weights $\le t<$ true weights, the optimum over splits of weight $>t$ is $\T$

checks.instances: 146 random stemmata, $5\le n\le7$ (binary and not), integer weights meeting the hypothesis
checks.result: restricted optimum is $\T$, uniquely, in all (all compatible sets enumerated); without the threshold the optimum differs from $\T$ in 78

results.label: prop:rooted
results.name: Rooted analogue
results.tested: the counting and maximality facts for clusters

checks.instances: 300 random rooted trees, $3\le n\le8$ ($\X$ adjoined)
checks.result: counting and maximality facts and the laminar bound hold in all

results.label: thm:pairwise
results.name: Pairwise bound
results.tested: the bound is at least the error probability of the estimator

checks.instances: 6 attraction-model instances meeting the hypotheses ($n=5,6$), two lengths each (bound $\approx0.5$ and $\approx0.05$, $L=40$--$1306$), $2\times10^4$--$4\times10^4$ simulated collations
checks.result: bound $\ge$ simulated $\Pr(\hat S_L\neq\T)$ (ties counted as errors) in all; largest ratio simulated/bound $0.198$

results.label: lem:gamma
results.name: Computing $\gamma$
results.tested: bisection on $g$ gives the margin of the ratio definition

checks.instances: 25 instances, $n=6$, all compatible sets enumerated, no solver
checks.result: bisection equals the ratio definition (tolerance $10^{-9}$, largest difference $1.0\times10^{-12}$)

results.label: thm:consistency
results.name: Consistency
results.tested: (a) the Bernstein and Hoeffding bounds dominate the error; (b) $\Pr(\hat S_L=\T)\to0$ when some $m(S)>m(\T)$

checks.instances: (a) 4 attraction-model instances with $\gamma=0.032$--$0.114$ ($n=5,6$), at the length where each bound first reaches $0.5$ ($L=301$--$7{,}031$), $2\times10^4$ collations; (b) a designed law and a long-branch instance with $m(S)>m(\T)$, $L=25$--$6{,}400$
checks.result: (a) both bounds $\ge$ simulated error in all (largest simulated error $0.0003$); (b) $\Pr(\hat S_L=\T)$ falls from $0.32$ to $0.00$ and $0.04$ to $0.00$

results.label: cor:samplesize
results.name: Sample size
results.tested: the length given by the formula makes the error at most $\varepsilon$

checks.instances: 236 (instance, $\varepsilon$) cases: attraction-model instances with $\gamma>0$ ($n=5,6$), $\varepsilon\in\{0.5,0.1,0.01,0.001\}$; 4 simulated at $\varepsilon=0.1$
checks.result: at the $L$ of the formula the Bernstein bound is $\le\varepsilon$ in all (largest ratio $0.239$); no error in the simulations at $\varepsilon=0.1$

results.label: prop:blocks
results.name: Dependent blocks
results.tested: with $J$ i.i.d.\ blocks and any dependence inside them, $2(n-3+K)e^{-J\gamma^2/2}$ dominates the error

checks.instances: 4 attraction-model instances ($n=5$, $\gamma=0.088$--$0.247$), blocks of $k=5$ identical units or $k=10$ units repeated with probability $1/2$, $J=122$--$951$ blocks, $10^4$ collations
checks.result: bound $\ge$ simulated error in all (at bound $\approx0.5$, simulated error $0.0000$ at most; with $k=20$ identical units and $J=10$--$320$, simulated error up to $0.697$, still below the bound); control: the i.i.d.\ bound with $L=Jk$ is exceeded by the simulated error in 4 of 12 short-$J$ cases

results.label: thm:gammaconf
results.name: Confidence bound for $\gamma$
results.tested: Clopper--Pearson $\gamma_{\mathrm{lo}}$ covers $\gamma$ with probability $\ge1-\delta$; no false certificate

checks.instances: two ten-witness regimes with exact $m$, $5$ lengths ($L=1{,}600$--$409{,}600$), $40$ collations each; the \emph{Lai}
checks.result: $\gamma_{\mathrm{lo}}\le\gamma$ in 400 of 400 collations (at least $95\%$ required at each length); every certified $\hat S_L$ is the true one; \emph{Lai}: $\hat S_L$ binary and optimal, $\gamma_{\mathrm{lo}}=-0.0236$, increasing with scaled length

results.label: prop:gammablocks
results.name: Certifying $\gamma$ with dependent units
results.tested: with blocks and Hoeffding intervals, $\gamma_{\mathrm{lo}}\le\gamma$ for all binary stemmata simultaneously with probability $\ge1-\delta$

checks.instances: 3 attraction-model instances on $n=5$ (two with $\gamma>0$, one long-branch with $\gamma<0$), $\delta=0.05,0.2$, $J=50,400,3{,}200$ blocks of $4$ units (identical, or repeated with probability $1/2$), $2{,}000$ collations each
checks.result: $\gamma_{\mathrm{lo}}(T)\le\gamma(T)$ for all $15$ binary stemmata simultaneously in every simulated collation (required $1-\delta$); no false certificate; the true stemma is certified in a fraction $0.00$ or less at $J=50$ and up to $1.00$ at $J=3{,}200$

results.label: thm:fragmentary
results.name: Fragmentary witnesses
results.tested: the two bounds of (b) and the sufficient condition of (c), under independent illegibility

checks.instances: 40 random rooted trees, $n=5$, random rates, $\alpha$ and independent illegibility; all innovation outcomes and legibility patterns enumerated
checks.result: proposals are restrictions; both bounds of (b) hold; in the 4 instances meeting the sufficient condition the true set is the unique maximum of $\tilde m$, and in all 39 with $\varrho>0$, rerun at $\delta=0.9\varrho/(4+2\mu)$

results.label: prop:textillegible
results.name: Illegibility that depends on the text
results.tested: the bounds of Theorem~\ref{thm:fragmentary}(b) with $\delta$, and the condition of (c), when illegibility depends on the readings

checks.instances: 48 random rooted trees ($n=5$: 30, $n=6$: 18), attraction model, all innovation outcomes; for each reading partition its own joint law of the illegible set (singletons, blocks, random mixtures, dependent across witnesses; on 12 trees, two witnesses illegible together exactly when they turn a proposed true split into a false one), every conditional rate $\le\delta$
checks.result: $\tilde m_\sigma\ge(1-4\delta)m_\sigma$ and $\tilde m_\tau\le m_\tau+2\delta\mu$ for every split (smallest slacks $4.0\times10^{-8}$, $7.8\times10^{-3}$); the independent-case bound with $\delta^{d}$ fails for 4 splits (control; 4 of them under the targeted laws); in all 36 instances with $\varrho>0$, rerun at $\delta=0.9\varrho/(4+2\mu)$, the true set is the unique maximum of $\tilde m$

results.label: thm:cuttingconsistency
results.name: Cutting-plane consistency
results.tested: the cutting-plane estimator maximises $M$ over trees and is consistent exactly when the true tree maximises $M$

checks.instances: (a) 33 random weighted collations, $n=5,6$; (b) the five-witness example; (c) 30 random rooted trees, $n=5$, all innovation states and legibility patterns
checks.result: (a) the maximum completable family has the weight of the best displaying tree; (b) uniquely best tree with a split never observed in full; (c) the inequality holds against every rival tree (smallest slack $0.07$)

checks.instances: six random rooted trees, $n=5$, attraction model with random illegibility, $M$ computed exactly; 100 collations per length
checks.result: true tree the unique maximum of $M$: selection frequency from $0.37$--$0.59$ at $L=25$ to $1.00$ at $L=1{,}600$; rival with larger $M$: falls to $0.00$

results.label: prop:dimfree
results.name: Tolerance independent of $n$
results.tested: the display probability of a false split by a rival tree is at most $2\max(\delta,2\delta^2)$, whatever $n$

checks.instances: 68 random binary trees $T'$ ($n=5$--$8$), all 2552 false splits, all legibility patterns, $\delta\in\{0.01,\dots,0.9\}$
checks.result: display probability $\le2\max(\delta,2\delta^2)$ in all (largest ratio 0.995); every displayed pattern leaves one of the four parts of the proof wholly illegible

results.label: prop:bediereffect
results.name: Bédier effect
results.tested: $\Pr(\hat S_L=\T)\le(1-m_\tau)^L$ (exact part); over-resolution on birth--death traditions

checks.instances: 6 attraction-model trees with a polytomy ($n=5,6$), the largest $m_\tau$ among false splits compatible with $\T$ ($0.012$--$0.066$), two lengths each ($L=11$--$194$), $2\times10^4$ collations
checks.result: $\Pr(\T$ is a maximiser$)\le(1-m_\tau)^L$ in all (ratio simulated/bound $0.00$--$0.58$)

checks.instances: index code on hand-made trees; the saved outputs of the three birth--death settings, all $\alpha$
checks.result: 62 assertions pass, 0 fail: truth inside the null band, raw optimum over-resolves, rival test and thresholds as stated, $P(\deg\ge3)$ ranges (orderings and bands only)

results.label: cor:tops
results.name: Polytomies that survive
results.tested: at a vertex of a rooted optimum with $k\ge3$ children, no union of two children is proposed

checks.instances: 400 random weightings on $n=5$, every optimum (505), 139 vertices with three or more children
checks.result: no union of two children has positive weight

results.label: thm:bedier
results.name: Bédier threshold
results.tested: the Kullback--Leibler bound dominates the error of the thresholded estimator; the second form dominates the first

checks.instances: 5 attraction-model trees with a polytomy ($n=5,6$) and $b>a$, $c=c^\ast$ and a random $c\in(a,b)$, at the length where the bound first reaches $0.5$ ($L=121$--$14{,}001$), $2\times10^4$ collations
checks.result: KL bound $\ge$ simulated $\Pr(\hat S_{L,c}\neq\T)$ in all (largest simulated error $0.1233$); at $c^\ast$ the KL bound is below the second form at every $L$ tested ($10$--$10^4$)

results.label: prop:gap
results.name: Largest-gap threshold
results.tested: deterministic step: under the hypothesis the largest gap separates true from false

checks.instances: 8{,}125 random instances meeting the hypothesis
checks.result: the cut separates true from false in all

results.label: prop:rival
results.name: Rival test
results.tested: given $w(\sigma)+w(\tau)=N$, $w(\sigma)$ is binomial with parameters $N$ and $m_\sigma/(m_\sigma+m_\tau)$

checks.instances: 4 attraction-model trees ($n=5,6$), a true split and its strongest crossing rival, $L=200$, $4\times10^4$ collations
checks.result: exact unit law: no unit proposes both; randomised probability-integral transform of $w(\sigma)$ given the sum, chi-square on deciles: $p=0.42$--$0.95$ under the binomial law, $p<10^{-6}$ for the control with the ratio raised by $15\%$
on the \emph{Lai} (computed, not a check), one-sided $p$ against the strongest rival: CDEFG $4.7\times10^{-7}$, CG $1.2\times10^{-41}$, DE $0.016$, DEF $0.049$

results.label: thm:mechanisms
results.name: Mechanisms of false support
results.tested: classification of outcomes with at most two innovations; two-sided bounds on every support

checks.instances: 40 random rooted trees, $n=5,6$, random rates and $\alpha$, all outcomes enumerated
checks.result: classification of all outcomes with at most two innovations, and the two-sided bounds on every support, hold in all

results.label: cor:dominance
results.name: Comparison of the codings
results.tested: at second order, the rooted support of each cluster of a split not of the tree is at most the unrooted support of the split

checks.instances: 60 random rooted trees ($n=5$--$7$, a third with polytomies), random rates, $\alpha\in\{0,1\}$ or random; all outcomes with at most two innovations; all 1396 splits not of the tree
checks.result: second-order rooted support of each cluster $\le$ unrooted support of the split in all (strict in 792); per outcome, a rooted proposal of $C$ or $D$ implies the unrooted proposal of $\tau$; the decomposition of the proof (disjoint pairs $\alpha^2$ against $1$, nested pairs $1-\alpha^2$ in both) equals the enumeration (largest difference $1.4\times10^{-17}$)

results.label: prop:modelbounds
results.name: Support bounds
results.tested: irreversible model, general $n$: the lower bound on true support and the upper bound on false mass

checks.instances: 60 random rooted trees, $n=6,7$, all mark patterns
checks.result: both bounds hold in all

results.label: cor:modelglobal
results.name: A sufficient condition
results.tested: under the hypothesis, global separation holds for the exact supports

checks.instances: 185 random rooted binary trees ($n=5$--$8$, rooted on an edge or at a vertex) with rates meeting the hypothesis; all $2^{|\mathcal E|}$ mark patterns enumerated
checks.result: global separation in all (smallest $\min_\T m-\max_\F m=6.3\times10^{-3}$), $\gamma>0$ for $n\le6$; of 756 instances missing the hypothesis, separation fails in 323

results.label: prop:quartet
results.name: Quartet
results.tested: the three formulas for the quartet supports of the irreversible model

checks.instances: 200 random rate vectors
checks.result: the three formulas equal exhaustive enumeration ($10^{-12}$)

results.label: cor:lba
results.name: Textual long-branch zone
results.tested: with $p_2=p_4=0$, $r_1=r_2=r$: consistency iff $(1-r)p_1p_3<r(2-p_1-p_3)$, and $13|24$ selected on the reverse side

checks.instances: 4210 points $(r,p_1,p_3)$, $p_2=p_4=0$: a grid, random points and 1000 within $10^{-9}$ of the boundary; and $300$ random general rate vectors; exact rational arithmetic
checks.result: the formulas of Proposition~\ref{prop:quartet} equal enumeration of the $2^6$ mark patterns at all 4510 points; $m_{12|34}>\max(m_{13|24},m_{14|23})$ exactly where $(1-r)p_1p_3<r(2-p_1-p_3)$ (2505 points) and $13|24$ strictly heaviest exactly on the reverse side (1165); neither at the 540 points of equality; 0 mismatches

results.label: thm:coding
results.name: Coding theorem
results.tested: the exact supports of the attraction model on the quartet, both codings

checks.instances: exact supports on the quartet (symbolic); $4\times10^5$ simulated units at a random parameter point
checks.result: reduce to Proposition~\ref{prop:quartet} at $\alpha=1$; Monte Carlo largest $|z|=1.58$ (fails at $5$)

results.label: prop:drift
results.name: Drift towards the root
results.tested: the exact supports on $(((1,3),2),4)$, both codings

checks.instances: exact supports (symbolic); $3\times10^5$ simulated units at a random point
checks.result: supports in $[0,1]$; Monte Carlo largest $|z|=1.82$ (fails at $5$)

results.label: prop:multistate
results.name: Several attractive readings
results.tested: with $A=\sum_ja_j^2$, the supports are those of the attraction model at $\alpha=\sqrt A$ up to $\Pr(|M|\ge3)$

checks.instances: 24 random rooted trees ($n=5,6$), $k\in\{2,3\}$ attractive readings, all outcomes enumerated
checks.result: two-innovation parts equal to those at $\alpha=\sqrt A$; $|m-m^{(\sqrt A)}|\le\Pr(|M|\ge3)$; dominance

results.label: prop:tworeading
results.name: Two-reading coding
results.tested: only coincidence proposes false splits at second order; the quartet supports and boundary

checks.instances: 24 random rooted trees ($n=5,6,7$), every outcome with at most two innovations; the quartet supports summed over all outcomes
checks.result: only disjoint pairs with both readings attractive propose a false split; $m_{13|24}=\alpha^2p_1p_3(1-r)^2$, $m_{14|23}=0$, $m_{12|34}=2r+O(\varepsilon^3)$

results.label: prop:alpha
results.name: Estimating $\alpha$
results.tested: $C^{(2)}=\alpha^2R^{(2)}$ for isolated pairs

checks.instances: 60 random rooted trees, $n=5..7$, 538 isolated pairs, all two-innovation outcomes
checks.result: $C^{(2)}=\alpha^2R^{(2)}$ exactly; data: shared-departure ratio $\hat C/\hat R$, Heinrichi $222/270=0.82$ (540 pairs isolated among the legible witnesses), \emph{Lai} $50/147=0.34$ (computed)

results.label: prop:polytomynull
results.name: Coincidence null at a polytomy
results.tested: the leading term of $m(\tau)$ at a polytomy, with an $O(\varepsilon^3)$ remainder

checks.instances: 60 random rooted trees with a polytomy ($k=3$ or $4$; 22 at the root), all $3^{|E|}$ innovation states at $\varepsilon=0.004$ and $0.002$
checks.result: the remainder divides by $7.8$--$8.1$ when $\varepsilon$ is halved (required $7$--$9$); median relative size $1.1\%$ (output). Not checked: $\kappa$, the overwrite case at $\alpha=1$, the estimators

results.label: sec:calibrated
results.name: Calibrated Bédier test, pruning rule
results.tested: every number and range stated for the pruning rule, on the saved outputs

checks.instances: the saved outputs, three $\alpha$ and $300$ traditions in each of the two settings
checks.result: 17 assertions on every number and range stated for the pruning rule pass, 0 fail (reconstruction only, no null rejection rate)

results.label: prop:size
results.name: Size
results.tested: the number of non-trivial splits is $2^{n-1}-n-1$

checks.instances: full conflict graphs on $n=4..7$ witnesses
checks.result: vertex counts $3,10,25,56$, equal to $2^{n-1}-n-1$

results.label: prop:crossing
results.name: Crossing set
results.tested: the true splits crossed by a false $\tau=A|B$ are the internal edges of $T[A]\cap T[B]$, non-empty and connected

checks.instances: 120 random binary trees, $n=5..9$, all 10{,}274 false splits
checks.result: crossing set equals $T[A]\cap T[B]$, non-empty and connected, in all

results.label: prop:five
results.name: Five witnesses
results.tested: the conflict graph on five witnesses is $L(K_5)$, neither chordal nor perfect

checks.instances: the full conflict graph on five witnesses
checks.result: isomorphic to $L(K_5)$ and to the complement of the Petersen graph; induced $C_4$ and $C_5$, not chordal

results.label: thm:fpt
results.name: Dynamic programme
results.tested: the $O(3^n)$ dynamic programme returns the maximum-weight compatible set

checks.instances: 40 random instances, $n=5..8$ (and $32$ more, $n=7,10$, in the margin check)
checks.result: the dynamic programme equals an exact MWIS (CP-SAT) in all

results.name: Birth--death traditions
results.tested: the metrics on hand-made trees, and the orderings and bands stated, on the saved outputs

checks.instances: index code on hand-made trees; the saved outputs of the three birth--death settings, all $\alpha$
checks.result: 62 assertions pass, 0 fail: truth inside the null band, raw optimum over-resolves, rival test and thresholds as stated, $P(\deg\ge3)$ ranges (orderings and bands only)
